entry.summary: More information about the GTA VI soundtrack has leaked. So far, only a select few songs from the 34-track LP have been announced, including “Flower In A Hurricane,” the Justice x Tame Impala x SZA x King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard collaboration that recently earned King Gizz their first-ever Hot 100 entry. entry.content:
More information about the GTA VI soundtrack has leaked. So far, only a select few songs from the 34-track LP have been announced, including “Flower In A Hurricane,” the Justice x Tame Impala x SZA x King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard collaboration that recently earned King Gizz their first-ever Hot 100 entry. Now, however, a newly leaked image of the album’s vinyl tracklist — which Rolling Stone confirms is legit — has revealed additional artists, including Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa, Arca, Fcukers, Zara Larsson, and Justice featuring the recently in-the-news Michael McDonald, among others.

Del Rey has further involvement with GTA VI: A month ago it was revealed that she would co-host one of the game's in-game radio stations with her husband and Morgan Wallen.

Other artists reportedly featured on the tracklist include Omar Apollo, Kali Uchis & Helado Negro, Rose Gray, Don Toliver, Tee Grizzley, Gunna, Burna Boy, Young Thug, Kodak Black, Camila Cabello, Cardi B, Rina Sawayama, and Playboi Carti. Earlier this week, Tove Lo shared her contribution "Blood In Your Eyes."

The game drops Thursday, with the full soundtrack set to arrive the following day. On Saturday Nov. 21, a Miami festival featuring artists from the soundtrack, including Cardi B, Kodak Black, and Don Toliver, is also scheduled to take place. On Dec. 11, a 50-song original score by Justice will be released — a separate release from the soundtrack album.

entry.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week
entry.summary: Every week the Stereogum staff chooses the five best new songs of the week. The eligibility period begins and ends Thursdays right before midnight. entry.content:
Every week the Stereogum staff chooses the five best new songs of the week. The eligibility period begins and ends Thursdays right before midnight. You can hear this week’s picks below and on Stereogum’s Favorite New Music Spotify playlist, which is updated weekly. (An expanded playlist of our new music picks is available to subscribers on Spotify and Apple Music, updated throughout the week.)

5

Kristin Hersh - "Pass Christian"

"This is sunshine in a jar." That's what Kristin Hersh's words say, anyway. Her voice says something else. For decades, Hersh has been one of left-of-center rock music's great spirit summoners, an otherworldly warbler with a cutting wit and a taste for the expansive. On a track that might as well be a throwaway — the lead single from the vinyl-only post-album EP — Hersh takes us on one of her heaviest trips yet. Per the credits, Hersh played every instrument on "Pass Christian," and she made her fuzz-drenched space-rock leads drip with as much dread as her voice. It's like she suddenly decided to make her own Earth-style drone-blues-metal and succeeded wildly. When she harmonizes with herself on the chorus, the beauty makes through, so maybe it really is sunshine in a jar. —Tom

4

Palehound - "Natural Disasters"

"Natural Disasters" is one of those songs that puts everything in perspective. Things are really bad — can’t we all just get through it together? El Kempner puts it in much more poignant terms: "There is no time to left to judge when/ Natural disasters are closing in on us/ And you’re still holding a fucking grudge.” The music is understated, built around a woven melody of guitar plucks and soft piano embellishments. It grows subtly, with shuffling drums, claps, and the occasional bell ring. Kempner sings of happiness at a distance, of finding peace in boundaries. It’s not a flashy ode that hammers home its sentiment, but rather one delivered with a compassionate, somewhat pragmatic sensibility. Even in its seeming simplicity, the song showcases the power of Kempner’s writing.

“Natural Disasters” isn’t a holiday song. But as the end of the year approaches and winter brings on its familiar self-reflection, just as we all reach peak exhaustion, the song feels timely. I’d hate to end this blurb with some yada yada about forgiveness and grace being bigger than any manmade weapons, vices, or treacheries. But if the world’s going to hell anyway, wouldn’t it be nicer to go peacefully than begrudgingly? —Margaret

3

Deloyd Elze - "Yamaha 250"

Deloyd Elze likes to mix up genres, bringing subtle electronics into tender alt-country. Might as well mix up spiritual traditions too, bragging to his lover about arranging a tarot reading right after introducing the refrain, "You set the table/ And I'll say grace." Allen's new song "Yamaha 250" is rich with that kind of lyrical playfulness, and maybe even richer on a musical level. As layers of skittering electronics and rustic strings pile up into gorgeous swells of emotion, so do memorable lines and character flourishes. It's a slice-of-life song that doubles as the sound of a promising musical artist making the leap. —Chris

2

Quiet Light - "Forever"

Quiet Light’s Blue Angel Sparkling Silver 2 made a splash this year because its 12 tracks feel like a soft, bright glimpse into the future of music. But Riya Mahesh’s new tune, “Forever,” is an odyssey back to the ’80s. It’s a sprawling synth-pop love song adorned with dreamy saxophone and a simple but evocative refrain: "All I wanna do is be good to you." More than anything, Quiet Light knows how to transform an emotion into a song, and "Forever" is pure love. —Danielle

1

Armand Hammer - "Assembly Lines"

On this week's surprise-dropped Snakes & Ladders, Armand Hammer haven't lost a step. E L U C I D and billy woods remain masters of abstract sounds and dystopian visions, not least of all on "Assembly Lines." Over Preservation's eerie synth soundscape, the rappers interrogate the intersection of labor and technology in the AI era, coming away with chilling conclusions about workers' fate: "My country, 'tis of thee/ Slavecatcher androids hunt you in electric sheep." —Chris

entry.title: The Mighty Mighty Bosstones Announce Reunion Show
entry.summary: Ska-punk hitmakers the Mighty Mighty Bosstones started way back in the early ’80s and hit a serious career peak in the late ’90s. They kept it going for a long time after that, too. The band finally broke up in 2022 without explanation, and it was pretty easy to speculate that frontman Dicky Barrett’s anti-vaccine…
entry.content:
Ska-punk hitmakers the Mighty Mighty Bosstones started way back in the early '80s and hit a serious career peak in the late '90s. They kept it going for a long time after that, too. The band finally broke up in 2022 without explanation, and it was pretty easy to speculate that frontman Dicky Barrett's anti-vaccine campaigning had something to do with their decision to call it quits.

Barrett co-wrote a song with Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. to promote one of Kennedy's anti-vaxxer rallies in DC and became a very visible all-around vaccine denier. That position cost Barrett his longtime job as the announcer and Jimmy Kimmel Live!, and he went on to start a band called the Defiant with a bunch of other guys who'd been kicked out of prominent punk bands, seemingly for being anti-vaxxers. But apparently, the Bosstones have figured things out, or at least agreed that their offers are generous enough to let the anti-vaxxer stuff slide.

About a year ago, Barrett joined the Boston hardcore band Haywire for a Bosstones cover, and he's been talking lately about trying to get the band back together. Next spring, British second-wave ska greats Madness will play the Hollywood Bowl. The openers include the Bosstones, along with fellow '90s ska-punk bands Dance Hall Crashers, Goldfinger, and Reel Big Fish. It's going down May 8. If you still haven't caught COVID yet, maybe you can go to that show and pick it up pick it up pick it up.

entry.title: Veeze – “guillermoandrade”
entry.summary: Back in May, the Detroit rap cult hero Veeze got sick of hearing people ask when he’ll drop the follow-up to his much-loved 2023 album Ganger, and he surprise-released an 11-song data-dump mixtape called Y’all Won. That was pretty fun — a new music release, presented as a passive-aggressive get-off-my-back gesture. Now, Veeze has a…
entry.content:
Back in May, the Detroit rap cult hero Veeze got sick of hearing people ask when he'll drop the follow-up to his much-loved 2023 album Ganger, and he surprise-released an 11-song data-dump mixtape called Y'all Won. That was pretty fun — a new music release, presented as a passive-aggressive get-off-my-back gesture. Now, Veeze has a new proper single, and this one feels a little less like someone had to pry it out of him.

Veeze's new song "guillermoandrade" is as casual as the rest of his music, and its spacey, almost vaporwave beat nicely aligns with his groggy mutter. Supposedly, it's inspired by the designer Guillermo Andradeis. It's about two minutes long, and it suddenly cuts off mid-line, but it's apparently being treated as a single and not a snippet. Mysterious! Check it out.

Just last week, Veeze also appeared on fellow detroit rapper Babyface Ray's single "Nigel Sylvester." The new Babyface Ray album Unfuckwithable 2 is out today, and I feel compelled to tell you that it has a Babyface Ray/Babyface collaboration. Amazing things happening. Here's the "Nigel Sylvester" video.

Unfuckwithable 2 is out now on Wavy Gang/EMPIRE. "guillermoandrade" is out now on Navy Wavy/Warner.

entry.summary: Last year, Scottish rock group Brògeal released a very solid debut album, Tuesday Paper Club, and we dubbed them one of the Best New Artists of 2025. Today, they’ve returned with a new single for the holidays. It’s called “The Last Noel” and features fellow Scottish singer-songwriter Rianne Downey. There are jingle bells! There’s accordion!…
entry.content:
Last year, Scottish rock group Brògeal released a very solid debut album, Tuesday Paper Club, and we dubbed them one of the Best New Artists of 2025. Today, they've returned with a new single for the holidays. It's called "The Last Noel" and features fellow Scottish singer-songwriter Rianne Downey. There are jingle bells! There's accordion! There's melancholy! It feels like a modern classic, with potent storytelling about past lovers.

In a press release, the band shared:

"The Last Noel" is a new offering as a Classic Scottish Christmas song. The tale is told between a man and a woman who haven’t seen each other in quite some time, it is unbeknownst to the couple whether the other is still in love or even still breathing. Every year when the nights turn cold and the Christmas decorations are put up around town and appear down from the loft, the memories of love from previous years come flying back. It also brings back a bitter twinge of the end times of a relationship, and memories are cast back to 'The Last Noel.' The song is a classic tale of love, loss and nostalgia set at Christmas time.

Listen below.

entry.content:
Winston Hightower, the Columbus lo-fi mainstay and Soul Glo member, earned Album Of The Week honors with this year's 100 Acre Wood. That record's guitar-based lo-fi indie-pop made it a perfect match for K Records. But Hightower contains multitudes, and his new project veers in a completely different direction.

Hightower has two new tracks out today under the name Hi-NRG! Both songs, "Handsome Daughter" and "Free Roof, On The House," are electronic pop excursions built on hyperactive rhythms. There's some woozy, pitched-up rapping on the latter song too, which pushes it over the top for me. Imagine an IDM Quasimoto, maybe?

It's always fun to hear an artist known for one kind of music throw themselves into another, and it's especially fun here. Check out both tracks below.

entry.title: 54 Ultra Shares Clairo Collab “Honeymoon”
entry.summary: Listen to Latin soul-inflected indie pop musician 54 Ultra's new single "Honeymoon," written and co-produced by Clairo.
entry.content:
JohnAnthony Rodriguez, the New Jersey singer/songwriter/producer who makes smooth, synthy, Latin soul-inflected indie-pop under the moniker 54 Ultra, has been picking up some buzz since his debut EP First Works dropped in 2025. His latest single, "Honeymoon," clearly has some industry firepower behind it, as Claire Cottrill — Clairo herself! — wrote it and produced it alongside Paul Cherry, Eddie Burns, and William Corduroy.

"Inspired by the sound of late '70s smoky pop music, 'Honeymoon' came together during a magical night at Electric Lady Studios in New York City," Rodriguez says. "I wanted to capture that feeling by recording straight to analog tape and using mostly vintage instruments and equipment, paying close attention to every detail along the way."

"I feel this song is a beautiful step in a new direction for me while still being familiar," he adds. "I even bought a Yamaha CP70 for this song to make sure I got the sound exactly where I wanted it to be. To me, it’s a perfect backdrop to the changing seasons into the end of the year." Listen below.

entry.title: Crate Release Debut Album, Stereogum Presents Release Show In Brooklyn Next Month
entry.summary: In 2024, the Brooklyn shoegaze band Crate released exactly one song, “Julia,” and we called it perfect. In 2025, they only released one more, “Necklace,” and we liked that one too. This year, new Crate music started trickling out, and now the floodgates are open: The band’s self-titled debut LP is out today. Produced by…
entry.content:
In 2024, the Brooklyn shoegaze band Crate released exactly one song, "Julia," and we called it perfect. In 2025, they only released one more, "Necklace," and we liked that one too. This year, new Crate music started trickling out, and now the floodgates are open: The band's self-titled debut LP is out today.

Produced by the band's Cody Hudgins and Gift's TJ Freda, Crate weaves the textures of classic shoegaze and slowcore into songs that shimmer and roar, languish and take flight. Songwriters Hudgins and Ezra Engler ensure there's substance beneath the gorgeous veneer, though the sheer beauty of the sound itself is enough to elicit an emotional response

It's an album worth celebrating, and we'll do just that next month in Brooklyn. Stereogum is presenting Crate's album release show Dec. 4 at ErF Studios with support from Whisper Doll, Club Ecology, and Nettle. Get tickets here, and stream the album below.

Crate is out now on Good English. Buy it here.

entry.summary: Brynne Mershon and Naomi Sullins are back with another wonderful Dovetail song. The Hudson Valley dream-pop/indie-folk duo shared “roadkill baby” a couple months ago, and now they’re releasing a vivid, lovesick ballad called “sunday night.” “‘sunday night’ is about accepting what’s been lost while still being tethered to it, and the pain of going back…
entry.content:
Brynne Mershon and Naomi Sullins are back with another wonderful Dovetail song. The Hudson Valley dream-pop/indie-folk duo shared "roadkill baby" a couple months ago, and now they're releasing a vivid, lovesick ballad called "sunday night."

"'sunday night' is about accepting what's been lost while still being tethered to it, and the pain of going back to something that does not feel entirely finished," the pair says about the track, which was written in spring of 2024. "The song's composition landed in a transitory period and holds within it transitory themes; the repeating refrain and droning chords seek to create an almost transcendent state, while still remaining grounded in earthy acoustic guitars, with touches of banjo."

Dovetail have always been skilled at conjuring immersive, emotional atmospheres, but the lyrics on "sunday night" are some of their best yet as they delve into storytelling: "That night I went to a party just for the background noise/ The stars told me that I'm alright as I tried to remember your voice." It's lonely, cosmic, and beautiful. Dive in below.

entry.title: Robyn Says Eurovision Is “Just Shit” Now: “It Really Is Embarrassing”
entry.summary: The entire history of Swedish pop music is all tied up with that of the Eurovision Song Contest. You could argue that the whole big-bang for Sweden’s pop dominance was in 1974, when ABBA’s “Waterloo” won Eurovision and rocketed the group to global stardom. But the current version of Eurovision holds absolutely no appeal for…
entry.content:
The entire history of Swedish pop music is all tied up with that of the Eurovision Song Contest. You could argue that the whole big-bang for Sweden's pop dominance was in 1974, when ABBA's "Waterloo" won Eurovision and rocketed the group to global stardom. But the current version of Eurovision holds absolutely no appeal for Swedish pop queen Robyn. Indeed, Robyn seems to really enjoy talking about how Eurovision sucks now.

In 2023, the Swedish artist Loreen won Eurovision, which meant that Sweden hosted the contest in 2024. When that happened, Robyn was one of more than 1,000 Swedish artists who signed an open letter demanding Israel's exclusion for Eurovision during its ongoing genocide of Palestinian people. But Eurovision has continued to include Israel, even as multiple countries boycott the competition in protest. As it turns out, though, Robyn's objection to Eurovision isn't strictly a genocide-related issue. She just doesn't like it.

Robyn is an elite podcast guest, which you already know if you heard her talking about hating Elon Musk on Las Culturistas earlier this year. Earlier this week, Robyn was on Amy Poehler's Good Hang podcast. Near the end of their interview, Poehler asked Robyn why Eurovision is such a big deal to Europeans, and Robyn immediately busted up laughing. She went on to sketch out Sweden's history of Eurovision greatness and to say that it's "just shit" now. She really put some mustard on the word "shit," too. Here's the full quote.

We don't have ABBA anymore, so I don't really watch Eurovision. They were one of the first people to win the whole thing for us, with "Waterloo." Hard to beat. Then we had [1991 winner] Carola; both me and Zara [Larsson] grew up listening to her. Amazing artist. Now, it's just shit, I would say.

I have American friends that I watch it with. My friend Bart has a blanket that he pulls up over his eyes while we're watching 'cause it's so embarrassing, and it really is embarrassing. And after I watched it, I feel really just overstimulated, and in a bad way. I was looking for words I'm not gonna say. But yeah, I don't like it.

It's a lot more charming to watch her say all that.

Check out the full episode below.

Robyn's very good album Sexistential is out now on Konichiwa/Young.

entry.summary: The Brooklyn-born, LA-based artist Zsela is the daughter of Chocolate Genius’ Marc Anthony Thompson and the half-sister of the movie star Tessa Thompson. As for Zsela, she has been making music for a long time, flitting around the outer edges of the music business and working with artists like A$AP Rocky and Actress. Her debut…
entry.content:
The Brooklyn-born, LA-based artist Zsela is the daughter of Chocolate Genius' Marc Anthony Thompson and the half-sister of the movie star Tessa Thompson. As for Zsela, she has been making music for a long time, flitting around the outer edges of the music business and working with artists like A$AP Rocky and Actress. Her debut album Big For You came out in 2024, and she'll follow it with a new one called The Party early next year.

Thus far, Zsela hasn't shared too many details about The Party. The album has nine tracks, but the tracklist that she shared today is mostly redacted. But we do know that it'll include at least tracks of breezy, Blood Orange-esque pop soul that refract pillowy '80s adult-contempo sounds through a circa-now prism.

Zsela co-wrote and co-produced her new single "Real Romantic" with Tinashe/Dijon collaborator Zack Sekoff, and the two of them also worked together on "Kinda Guy," which came out last month. Zsela and Sekoff made the whole album together, much of it in what a press release calls "a makeshift studio." Both of the singles radiate the same spacey, comfortable feeling, and they suggest that the full LP will make for luxurious vibe-out material. Listen to both below.

The Party is out 2/19 on Nice Life. Zsela will perform 11/19 at LA's 2220 Arts + Archives.

entry.content:
Back in April, the raggedly emotive Queens indie rockers Hiding Places released their debut album The Secret To Good Living. It's full of blown-out guitars and meditative vocals from Audrey Keelin, with bursts of bleary twang from fellow singer-songwriter Nicholas Byrne. The album is well worth hearing, as is "Paradise," a new Hiding Places single out today.

"Paradise" is on the softer side of Hiding Place's sound. The band members have separate interpretations of the song. Here's Keelin:

When we talked about the significance of this song together, our bandmate Michael said, "Paradise isn’t what it used to be." A face isn’t the same every time you look. Time passes. Change exists. This is a song that investigates making that personal realization in the eyes of the narrator.

And Byrne:

Paradise... does that mean it’s a place where all your desires ring true? Or is that place really a projection of all your fears, where every desire is an antidote. Making peace with change, that feels how I thought paradise would.

And here's another thought from Michael Matsakis:

A goal with the arrangement was to hold back in order to not let the song get too heavy too fast. I felt like a slow burn matched the energy of the song more than something that gets super big. We stripped down instrument parts to more basic melodic fragments and worked on intertwining non-melodic lines to form harmony.

Below, watch the "Paradise" video, directed by Hiding Places and Nara Avakina, and stick around for The Secret To Good Living if you like.

entry.title: The Edge Finally Breaks His Legendary Silence On Elf 2
entry.summary: A few says ago, the world learned something fascinating about the Edge, longtime guitarist for U2. The actor and former Conan O’Brien sidekick Andy Richter had a small role in Elf, Jon Favreau’s 2003 Christmas classic, and he co-wrote the new book Elf Unwrapped: Behind The Scenes Of A Modern Christmas Classic. During a couple…
entry.content:
A few says ago, the world learned something fascinating about the Edge, longtime guitarist for U2. The actor and former Conan O'Brien sidekick Andy Richter had a small role in Elf, Jon Favreau's 2003 Christmas classic, and he co-wrote the new book Elf Unwrapped: Behind The Scenes Of A Modern Christmas Classic. During a couple of interviews to promote the book, Richter claimed that the Edge had written an Elf sequel and that he took his movie idea to Shauna Robertson, one of the film's producers.

Richter told the Daily Beast's Obsessed podcast, "It was all about the evil South Pole elves kidnapping Santa or something like that." Sadly, the studios did not fast-track the Edge's Elf sequel, so it'll have to sit right next to Nick Cave's Gladiator sequel in the "unproduced scripts that exist, somehow" file. But fortunately, Richter broke this news during a U2 album rollout, which means that the Edge now has to answer questions about his potential Elf 2.

Today, U2's new album Carnaval De Luz is out in the world. As a result, the band sat down with broadcast journalist Anthony Mason (not the former NBA player) for this weekend's episode of CBS Sunday Morning. The episode hasn't aired yet, but CBS had to share the Edge's confirmation of the Elf story ahead of time.

When Mason asked Edge about his Elf sequel script, Edge calmly replied, "It's an outrage for someone to suggest that I would write a script. I wrote a treatment — it's a different thing — for my own amusement, yes." The best part of this is that Edge's U2 bandmates apparently had no idea about this Elf thing. They all thought it was pretty funny.

Apparently, this is something that the Edge sometimes does. He gets movie ideas, and he writes them down: "This happened to me about three or four times. I will wake up, and I will have a complete movie outline in my head. This morning, I woke up with this idea in my head for a sequel to Elf." He aded that he thinks the original Elf is "incredible."

But Edge didn't just write this treatment for his "own personal amusement." He also took it to Shauna Robertson and set a meeting: "I talked to a friend who's a film producer... I think I just shared it with a couple of people. Honestly, I thought it was so far-fetched that I didn't take it terribly seriously. But you never know."

The timeline of the Edge's screenwriting ambitions aren't quite clear from the interview, but he might've written his treatment during COVID. (He doesn't comment on what it was about, so "South Pole elves" is all we knew.) If Edge did write it around 2020, even if his potential screenplay had been rushed into production, it wouldn't have come out until Elf was more than 20 years old and many of its stars were dead. So that's one potential issue with the Edge's Elf sequel. But like the man says, you never know. Many amateur screenwriters have movie-sequel ideas, but most of them aren't in one of the biggest bands of all time. If you're the Edge, you can get someone on the phone.

You can see this riveting exchange for yourself below.

entry.title: Ethel Cain & Robin Carolan – “Wynter Waxeth”
entry.summary: Hear Ethel Cain and composer Robin Carolan's original song in Middle English for Robert Eggers' upcoming horror film'Werwulf.'
entry.content:
Werwulf, the latest painstakingly researched period gothic horror film from The VVitch/Nosferatu director Robert Eggers, is arriving next month. Robin Carolan, the Tri Angle record label founder and composer who scored Eggers' last two movies, provided its soundtrack, and he enlisted Ethel Cain for the original song "Wynter Waxeth." Werwulf is set in 14th-century England, so naturally Cain sings the track in era-appropriate Middle English. Cain explains:

It's always been my dream to score a horror film in some way, and I couldn't think of a more perfect first opportunity than getting to work with Rob and Robin on a song for Werwulf. We were immediately creatively aligned so the entire process felt very intuitive and natural. It felt like I was back in the heart of the music I started off making at the beginning of my career, which felt really good to return to. Robin sent me a bunch of old medieval music at the beginning and was very into the psaltery, which introduced me to the traditional instrument. I bought one online and wound up plucking out this simple little harp line on it and that’s where the song began.

Carolan adds:

I'd send [Ethel Cain] medieval music, prayers, weird ambient stuff, and we'd talk through it all. It was one of those rare collaborations where we just seemed to be on the same page about everything. Initially we'd talked about her contributing vocals to the score in a more textural way, but it wasn't long until we started discussing a full blown song. Her talent and open mindedness to try different things is honestly incredible. She sang the song in Middle English, and with Rob's help she mastered the pronunciation on the hop, practically in one session. She brought so much earthy, feral, haunted beauty to the score, and it's hard to imagine it without her presence.

entry.title: 2026 Latin Grammy Winners Include Rosalía, Fred Again.., & Congressman-Elect Bobby Pulido
entry.summary: Rosalía is getting her flowers this week. On top of being the subject of a new U2 song, last night, she swept at the Latin Grammys. She won five awards for her LUX oeuvre — Album Of The Year, Song Of The Year (“La Perla”), Best Pop Song (also “La Perla”), Best Alternative Music Album,…
entry.content:
Rosalía is getting her flowers this week. On top of being the subject of a new U2 song, last night, she swept at the Latin Grammys. She won five awards for her LUX oeuvre — Album Of The Year, Song Of The Year ("La Perla"), Best Pop Song (also "La Perla"), Best Alternative Music Album, and Best Short Form Music Video (for "Sauvignon Blanc," directed by Noah Dillon). LUX also won for Best Engineered Album, which went to her team of recording and mastering engineers. This year's recognition makes Rosalía the first woman to win the Latin Grammy for Album Of The Year three times; she previously won for 2018's El Mal Querer and 2022's Motomami. She also opened the show, performing a medley of “La Rumba del Perdón,” “La Perla” and “Dios Es Un Stalker.”

Edgar Barrera took home the Latin Grammy for Producer Of The Year, making him the most-awarded individual in Latin Grammy history, breaking a tie with Residente to reach 30 career wins.

Argentine rapper Milo J also won big, taking home four awards — Record Of The Year for "Niño," Best Urban Performance for "Gil" with Trueno, Best Folk Album and Best Recording Package for La Vida Era Más Corta. He also performed “Solifican12” and “Gil" at the event.

Another major performance came from Puerto Rican reggaeton legend Daddy Yankee, who was honored as Person Of The Year, days after being revealed as a special guest at next year's Coachella. Janet Jackson, who collaborated with Yankee on the 2018 single "Made For Now," made a surprise appearance to present.

Daddy Yankee's performance celebrated decades of hits, including 2019's "Con Calma," 2018's "Dura," his 2017 hit Luis Fonsi collaboration "Despacito," 2005's "Rompe," this year's "POKITO" and, of course, 2004's "Gasolina," for which he was joined by LL Cool J, who interwove his hit "Mama Said Knock You Out." Daddy Yankee also brought out Argentine producer Bizarrap, Spanish hitmaker Bad Gyal, and Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh.

Last week Bobby Pulido flipped a seat in Texas’ 15th Congressional District, and last night, he won his third Latin Grammy for Best Tejano Album. In his acceptance speech, he reiterated his retirement from music but said, “Tejano music is in very good hands.”

Another unexpected takeaway from the evening is that Sting and Fred again.. are now Latin Grammy winners. Yes, all thanks to experimental rap duo CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, who took home three awards for Best Long For Music Video for "Free Spirits," Best Electronic Music Performance for "Beto's Horns - Fred Remix" with Fred again.., and Best Pop/Rock Song for "Hasta Jesús Tuvo Un Mal Día" featuring Sting.

Check out clips from the night below.

entry.title: IDK – “Welcome” (Feat. Eminem & Prod. J Dilla)
entry.summary: Eminem and J Dilla both came from the same Detroit underground rap scene in the ’90s, but they never worked together. Dilla did work with Proof, Em’s late mentor and fellow D12 member. For a little while, Proof and Dilla had a duo called the Funky Cowboys. But Eminem himself never rapped on a Dilla…
entry.content:
Eminem and J Dilla both came from the same Detroit underground rap scene in the '90s, but they never worked together. Dilla did work with Proof, Em's late mentor and fellow D12 member. For a little while, Proof and Dilla had a duo called the Funky Cowboys. But Eminem himself never rapped on a Dilla beat, until today, two decades after Dilla's death. The person who finally brought them together is the the Maryland rapper IDK.

IDK has picked up a great many co-signs from legends. Earlier this year, he released his concept album E.T.D.S. – Even The Devil Smiles, featuring collaborations with people like Pusha T, Black Thought, and the RZA, as well as posthumous appearances from MF DOOM and DMX. A few months later, he appeared alongside Peter Gabriel on Everything Is Recorded's "Beyond The Brilliant Haze." Today, he releases "Welcome," a new Eminem collab built on production that Dilla left behind, and it's coming out on Em's Shady label.

Eminem really only does the hook on "Welcome," but it's fascinating to hear him adjust his ultra-precise meter to Dilla's signature drag. IDK comes off well on the track, too. Here's what he says about the track:

When I first started working on this music, I remember looking up at my ceiling and saying "thank you." I was speaking to Dilla because it felt like everything that could have been, in a way, started to clear itself organically. I knew this was an important opportunity and a statement for hip-hop itself.

The first rap album I’ve ever owned was 50 Cent’s Get Rich Or Die Tryin’. A Shady Records release. The first raps I made it a point to memorize were Eminem raps. I’ve been at it for some time now, so to be at the point in my journey seems surreal. I’m excited for this next chapter in my career.

IDK, Eminem, and director Vuhlandes shot the "Welcome" video in Detroit, and there's also a short documentary clip with footage of IDK and Eminem in the studio together. Check out both below.

"Welcome" is out now on Shady/Interscope.

entry.title: Mike Watt, Patrick Shiroishi, Eli Winter, & Lily Finnegan Form New Supergroup, Announce Debut Album Bonsai Weeping Willow
entry.summary: Here’s a fun surprise: A fasinating crew of accomplished musicians across the realm of rock, jazz, folk, and experimental music have assembled to make an album called Bonsai Weeping Willow. The project brings together bassist Mike Watt (of Minutemen/Dos/Firehose fame, plus a million other endeavors), saxophonist Patrick Shiroishi (of the Armed and a million other…
entry.content:
Here's a fun surprise: A fasinating crew of accomplished musicians across the realm of rock, jazz, folk, and experimental music have assembled to make an album called Bonsai Weeping Willow.

The project brings together bassist Mike Watt (of Minutemen/Dos/Firehose fame, plus a million other endeavors), saxophonist Patrick Shiroishi (of the Armed and a million other endeavors), drummer Lily Finnegan (of Heat On and a million other endeavors), and guitarist Eli Winter (who you may know from his solo work or, you guessed it, a million other endeavors). They haven't adopted a band name; instead, all four musicians are simply credited by their name.

Watt assembled the group, convening them in his hometown of San Pedro to record at Casa Hanzo, a studio run by Watt’s Secondmen bandmate Pete Mazich. With barely any time to get on each other's wavelengths, they tracked 90 minutes of overdub-free improvisational music, later culled into tracks by Winter. One of those, a nearly eight-minute excursion called "Deluxe Hook Package," is out today, so listen to it below.

No word on a tracklist or pre-order link yet, but the album will be out on 2/1.

It’s about a nightclub promoter who suddenly learns that he has a 10-year-old son who…
entry.content:
Jordan Firstman, the comedian and actor from I Love LA and English Teacher, is the writer, director, and star of Club Kid, a new indie film that's been picking up serious buzz since it debuted at Cannes earlier this year. It's about a nightclub promoter who suddenly learns that he has a 10-year-old son who he has to take care of, and I have only heard good things about it. Club Kid is finally getting its theatrical release this weekend, and A24 Music has surprise-released a new tie-in EP that features a couple of Arthur Russell covers.

The Club Kid EP has five songs. Three of them are actual club tracks that appear to be entirely new, and those selections come from Shygirl, Brutalismus 3000, and Moby. The film also reportedly features a needledrop of "The Boy With A Smile," a song that the late Arthur Russell probably recorded around 1985 but which didn't come out until the posthumous 2023 album Picture Of Bunny Rabbit. The EP has two different covers of that song — one from Christine And The Queens and another from Nirosta Steel, the Russell collaborator who became much more prominent after his own collection My Skyscraper came out earlier this year. Below, check out the Club Kid soundtrack EP and the trailer for the film.

Club Kid is in theaters now, and the tie-in EP is out on A24 Music.
